title: v1.24.0
featureLines: Undock: launch as a floating transparent window from a web page or a native app (`displayxr-view:` protocol; first command line for this viewer: positional scene path, `--transparent/--rect/--src`), download toast, single-instance hand-o…
Command line, where there was none before: a positional scene path plus `--transparent`, `--rect`, `--src` and `--vh`, parsed before anything else starts (#99)
`displayxr-view:` protocol handler — the viewer registers the scheme itself at launch, so a page or a native app can spawn it directly (#99)

Single-instance hand-off: a second launch of our own type passes its URL to the running instance over `WM_COPYDATA` instead of stacking a rival window; a foreign `type=` is forwarded to the sibling viewer (#99)
`--transparent` is a creation parameter, not a post-hoc toggle — the window is born shaped and topmost so it floats over the desktop from the first frame; Ctrl+T is unchanged (#99)
`--rect` places the window in physical virtual-screen pixels, clamped into the panel's monitor only when the runtime confirms it actually located a 3D panel (#99)
`--vh` pins the virtual display height as the launcher's statement about the asset, outranking auto-fit's guess from the bounding box (#99)
`--src=<url>` downloads on a detached worker into a per-user cache; the URL a redirect chain lands on is re-checked under the stricter protocol policy (#99)

title: v0.26.0
featureLines: The model viewer can now be **undocked** — launched as a floating, transparent
window straight from a web page or a native app, with its position, size and the
model it loads all set at launch. A page links `displayxr-view:` and the viewer
opens on top of it; a native app spawns the same thing with a handful of flags.
This release also adds a **studio lighting mode** and **4x MSAA**, so the floating
window reads as a finished object rather than an aliased cut-out.
It requires nothing new from the runtime — it runs against the runtime you already
have installed.

`debug.dxr.ev.key`.

title: DisplayXR Shell v2.2.0
featureLines: Voice control works again. A missing dependency ceiling let a new major of the
`mcp` Python package into the shipped voice runtime, where it wedged during
session initialization — voice appeared to start and then silently did nothing,
leaving an empty log behind. The runtime is now pinned to the major we test, and
a wedged voice process says so (in the log, and as a toast) instead of failing
invisibly. Voice reaches `[realtime] session ready` and push-to-talk arms.

title: DisplayXR Shell v2.1.0
featureLines: **Your title bar stays put.** The 3D window title bar could previously disappear for good — closing an app leaked its chrome slot, and a relaunch that reused the same client id inherited a dead, invisible swapchain. Both are fixed.

**The launcher's "+" tile no longer looks like a crash.** Picking an app to add opens the file dialog in front of the compositor instead of behind it, and the shell keeps running while the dialog is up.

**No more 5-second freeze on launch.** Starting a 2D or unknown-type app used to block the whole workspace while the shell slept and polled; launches are now detected on the regular frame tick, so the workspace stays live.
**Overlays survive a bad frame.** The taskbar, launcher, toasts, and cursor no longer risk going dark permanently after a transient swapchain error.
**The shell notices when the runtime goes away.** If the runtime or session dies, the shell now exits cleanly instead of sitting inert against a dead service.
Runtime/session-loss detection — the shell shuts down cleanly when the runtime or OpenXR session goes away, rather than continuing to run against a dead service (#93)

`--workspace-action` is implemented per the workspace-controller contract, supporting `show-launcher`, `layout-grid`, and `layout-immersive`; unknown `--flags` are now rejected up front instead of being silently treated as app paths (#92)
App launching is detected on the per-frame tick instead of a blocking 5-second sleep-poll, so launching a 2D or unknown-type app no longer stalls the workspace (#95)
